newsitem.title: USA: U.S. senators ask Reno to sue tobacco companies.
newsitem.headline: U.S. senators ask Reno to sue tobacco companies.

text.p: Five Democratic senators Tuesday asked Attorney General Janet Reno to file suit against tobacco companies to recover the federal government's cost of treating smoking-related illnesses.
The senators, in a letter to Reno, estimated the federal government spent about $20 billion a year through Medicare, Medicaid and other federal programs on tobacco-related health costs.
"We are writing to strongly urge that you follow the lead of 23 attorneys general in seeking to recover the approximately $20 billion in tobacco-related costs," they said.
"We know that you have been considering options for legal action in this ara. We urge you to act promptly to have the federal government join the states in taking action," the letter said.

The letter comes amid negotiations between state attorneys general and tobacco companies. The firms hope to negotiate a settlement to state lawsuits asking them to pay the Medicaid costs of treating smoking-related illness.
The two sides are talking about a plan in which industry would provide up to $300 billion in compensation over 25 years and accept federal controls, in return for future immunity.
Democratic senators signing the letter were Tom Harkin of Iowa, Frank Lautenberg of New Jersey, Dick Durbin of Illinois, Paul Wellstone of Minnesota and Ron Wyden of Oregon.
At a news conference, several of the senators said they had not talked to Reno directly about the issue.
But they said they had been led to believe by Clinton administration staff aides that they would be supportive of the proposal.
